title: The GAGA margin needs an algebraic constructibility convention
body: The asserted “équivalence des catégories” of algebraic and analytic constructible torsion sheaves needs its constructibility convention recovered. On $\mathbb C$, the finite-coefficient sheaf supported on the closed discrete analytic set $\mathbb Z=V(\sin\pi z)$ is locally constant on that set and its complement, but its support is not algebraically constructible in $\mathbb A^1_{\mathbb C}$. Two possibly disconnected analytic strata already suffice; a connected-stratum convention instead allows a locally finite point stratification. This conditional support test leaves intact narrower comparison categories, such as finite local systems.

title: Wild coefficients obstruct the unrestricted open-immersion extension
body: If the proposed finite-type extension is read with unrestricted torsion, take $j:\mathbb G_m\hookrightarrow\mathbb A^1$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$ and coefficients $\mathbb F_p$. At the origin the Artin–Schreier classes $t^{-m}$, for $m>0$ prime to $p$, are linearly independent in the punctured strict-local $H^1$: a nonzero negative-valuation term $h^p-h$ has pole order divisible by $p$. The resulting infinite stalk of $R^1j_*\mathbb F_p$ prevents constructibility, so the purity restriction is essential even on a smooth curve where resolution itself is not the issue.
